estimand: Transfer to a new subject performing a stable, task-competent policy, without conflating transfer error with task acquisition or treatment changes.
evidence_hierarchy: Author-defined mature, expert, or late-stage criterion
Released stage, phase, or protocol metadata
Reproducible methods criterion established before the recorded task
Explicit pretraining before recording when the numerical criterion is unrecoverable
Unresolved when no defensible maturity evidence exists
guardrails: Never select a maturity cutoff using GRU or baseline performance.
Apply maturity and treatment filters before chronological reindexing and v1/v2 splitting.
Never adapt on one treatment and test on another.
Preserve within-session acquisition and reversal when it is the intended mature task dynamic.
Keep superseded all-session results only as labeled sensitivity or descriptive analyses.

datasets.label: Grossman (mouse)
datasets.evidence: The methods describe habituation, deterministic task training, and 90/10 training before the final task stage represented by the released behavioral cohort.
datasets.rule: Retain all released final-stage sessions; preserve current v1 odd/even chronological split.

datasets.label: Chen (mouse)
datasets.evidence: The paper states that mice learned the task before data collection, reached asymptotic performance, and showed no session effect on reward acquisition across the eight recorded sessions.
datasets.rule: Retain all eight recorded sessions per mouse; preserve current v1 split.

datasets.label: Zid (human)
datasets.evidence: Participants passed a 25-trial fixed-probability practice screen before the 300-trial main task. The adapter already excludes practice trials. Four constant-choice participants remain because they passed the task-understanding gate and their behavior is valid for prediction, although the paper excluded them from model-based analyses.
datasets.rule: Retain all 258 main-task sessions and the current v2 first-half/second-half split.

datasets.label: Lebedeva (mouse)
datasets.evidence: Mice progressed through deterministic, 90/10, and 80/20 training over 4-12 weeks; recording began only after the experimenters judged proficiency. Every released mouse has at least 26 recording sessions.
datasets.rule: Retain all released recording sessions; preserve current v1 split.

datasets.label: Beron (mouse)
datasets.evidence: The paper describes behavior after extensive training and reports stable behavioral features within and across released sessions. No numerical proficiency cutoff is recoverable.
datasets.rule: Retain all released final-task sessions; preserve current v1 split.

datasets.label: Kwak (mouse)
datasets.task: Dynamic two-arm bandit under D1/D2 manipulation
datasets.evidence: All mice were over-trained on the dynamic task for approximately three weeks before injections. Each mouse then contributed ten DMSO and ten CNO sessions.
datasets.rule: Filter to DMSO sessions first, reindex the ten DMSO sessions chronologically, then assign odd positions to adaptation and even positions to test.
datasets.existing_results: quarantined: the current generic split adapts on CNO and tests on DMSO

datasets.label: Miller (rat)
datasets.evidence: The paper reports that rats performed the task, but neither the release nor the methods provide a recoverable proficiency threshold, training-stage label, or prespecified mature-session boundary for the 1,857 retained sessions.
datasets.rule: Do not invent a session cutoff. Seek author clarification or session-stage metadata before mature-primary use.
datasets.existing_results: retain as explicitly labeled all-session sensitivity only

datasets.label: Findling (human)
datasets.evidence: Before the two experimental days, participants completed two 60-trial familiarization runs containing reversals. The released analytic cohort contains the six experimental scanning runs per participant.
datasets.rule: Retain all six experimental runs per participant; preserve current v1 split.

datasets.label: Tang (macaque)
datasets.evidence: Both monkeys were trained before implantation and recording, including training to complete approximately 24 blocks per session. The release contains eight neurophysiology recording sessions.
datasets.rule: Retain all eight recording sessions. Preserve intended within-block acquisition and reversal dynamics and the current v1 split.
datasets.existing_results: reusable; descriptive tier remains appropriate because n=2

datasets.label: Alsiö (rat)
datasets.task: Visual/spatial discrimination and reversal under pharmacology
datasets.evidence: Touchscreen pretraining had explicit criteria, but the admitted cohorts II-V are the subsequent drug-administered novel-pair acquisition and reversal experiments themselves. The release includes multiple drug families and does not represent repeated samples from one stable untreated policy.
datasets.rule: Do not derive a post hoc mature subset from experimental acquisition/reversal sessions. A future treatment-specific analysis would need a separately defined estimand and complete condition metadata.
datasets.existing_results: retain as descriptive all-condition sensitivity only

datasets.label: Eckstein (human)
datasets.evidence: Before the 120-trial main task, participants completed a three-step tutorial with deterministic, switching, and stochastic instructions and practice. The released canonical trials are the main task, not tutorial trials.
datasets.rule: Retain all 306 released main-task sessions and the current v2 first-half/second-half split; continue disclosing the paper's analytic n=291 discrepancy.

datasets.label: Costa (macaque)
datasets.evidence: Monkeys were trained until they routinely completed 15-20 blocks per session with stable performance across three schedules; training sessions were excluded from the reported analyses.
datasets.rule: Retain all released stochastic testing sessions. Lesion group is fixed between subjects, so no subject crosses treatment between adaptation and test; retain the existing stress-test tier.

datasets.label: López-Yépez (mouse)
datasets.evidence: Mice completed two training stages before variable-interval testing and advanced after exceeding 80% correct lit-port choices. The release contains the subsequent testing sessions.
datasets.rule: Retain all released variable-interval testing sessions; preserve current v1 split and the existing stress-test tier.

datasets.label: Hattori (mouse)
datasets.task: Baited probabilistic reversals during longitudinal OFC imaging
datasets.evidence: The paper defines days 1-14 as early behavior and day 15 onward as late/expert-stage behavior. The adapter already applies this author-defined boundary to the untreated longitudinal imaging cohort before splitting.
datasets.rule: Retain each mouse's 15th probabilistic-reversal session onward, then recompute chronological v1 odd/even membership within the retained sequence.
